inputs.text: Activists in Uttar Pradesh are spot on when they point out the government's failure to put in place any workable process for brick kiln operators to get environmental clearances, even three months after it was supposed to start. This isn't just some bureaucratic mess—it's proof that our institutions are designed to protect the powerful and wealthy at the expense of vulnerable communities, leading to ongoing environmental harm and deepening the inequality that comes from historical power imbalances. The brick kiln owners have State Pollution Control Board approvals for water and air standards, and they're saying they're ready to comply as long as the process gets fixed and the middlemen tied to systemic corruption are removed. Legal experts are calling for the state to follow through on court decisions and build a real approval framework. We need urgent structural reforms right now to protect marginalized groups from being sacrificed to this profit-driven inaction.
